question: Assume today is 2026-08-25. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births in Japan in July 2026, as first reported in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's preliminary monthly vital statistics (which also count foreign nationals in Japan).

target.what: Number of live births occurring in Japan in July 2026 among all persons in Japan, including foreign nationals, as first published in the MHLW preliminary monthly vital statistics.
target.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), Japan
target.cadence: Monthly preliminary vital statistics (人口動態統計速報), typically released with roughly a two-month lag; the first July 2026 report is expected after the 2026-08-25 cutoff.
target.caveats: Working interpretation: live births by date of birth/occurrence, not stillbirths, compiled from notifications received by the preliminary compilation cutoff, and including foreign nationals in Japan. The first preliminary figure may be incomplete and later revised. If the relevant MHLW table exclude

candidates.perspective: MHLW monthly vital statistics time series
candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 preliminary births should be near recent July preliminary levels adjusted for the declining trend and for 2026 Hinoeuma effects; prior July values and 2026 Jan-Jun values anchor the level, seasonality, and volatility.
candidates.data_to_find: MHLW 人口動態統計速報 monthly birth counts for July 2018-2025, preferably first preliminary and revised figures, and Jan-Jun 2026 monthly births. Record whether foreign nationals are included and compute July/June and July/January ratios.

assessment.note: The July total-population series cleanly decomposes into Japanese and foreign components: p45 is p43 plus p39 for July 2024, and p46 is p44 plus p40 for July 2025. p1 is the MHLW Japanese-only July 2025 figure and is essentially the same level as p44, supporting use of the stat.go.jp total series as an all-person July baseline.

p13 and p14 report only 3 foreign births in July 2025 and 7 cumulative Jan-Jul 2025, far below the stat.go.jp foreign live-birth series p39-p42. The p13/p14 rows are mis-scoped or otherwise unusable as national foreign births and should not be used.

The 2026 signals are not independent: p16, p33 and p35 are the same January 2026 +0.5% yoy signal; p54/p55 show Jan-May cumulative +0.4%; p52/p53 show May 2026 -1.7%; p56/p57 show trailing 12-month -0.4%. They overlap in the same MHLW preliminary system and describe different periods, so they indicate trend uncertainty rather than a single contradiction.

The 1966 Hinoeuma decline is about -25% (p38 and duplicates), but modern survey evidence shows most respondents would not avoid a 2026 birth (p24), only a minority were advised to avoid (p26), and many are merely aware of the superstition (p27). The historical analogue is not directly transferable; p18 also indicates today's mothers are older than in 1966, further weakening the analogue.

These support a May-to-July seasonal bridge: p52 is May 2026 total births, p53 is May 2025 total births, and p46 is July 2025 total births. The same all-person definition is used, so the May/July ratio can be transferred, subject to seasonality risk.

These provide alternative 2026 trend anchors for scaling July 2025 total births: Jan-May cumulative growth (p54/p55) and trailing 12-month growth (p56/p57). They overlap in time and source, so agreement would not be independent confirmation.

methods.rationale: Uses the most recent observed July all-person total, July 2025 p46, as the 2026 baseline. This is a no-trend anchor; it will be penalized in backtests if the recent declining trend persists. It uses stat.go.jp population-estimate births rather than MHLW preliminary births, but the definitions are close for all-person live births.

Scales July 2025 total births p46 by the Jan-May 2026/2025 cumulative ratio (p54/p55). This transfers the early-2026 cumulative trend to July. Main failure mode: Hinoeuma effects or reporting timing may differ between the Jan-May cumulative period and July; shares p54/p55 with m5.

methods.rationale: Adjusts July 2025 total births by the trailing 12-month growth rate (p56/p57), a smoother recent trend signal than a single month. Failure mode: the trailing period ends in May 2026 and does not include July 2026, so any July-specific Hinoeuma or reporting effect is missed.

assumptions.name: July 2026 Hinoeuma/timing deviation factor relative to Jan-May 2026 trend
assumptions.rationale: The Jan-May 2026 cumulative all-person series is already +0.4% yoy (p54/p55), so any Hinoeuma effect in early 2026 births is muted. Survey evidence shows 76.2% would not avoid a 2026 birth (p24), only 12.4% were advised to avoid (p26), and 5.2% deliberately chose a 2026 birth (p25); the historical 1966 -25% decline (p38) is not directly transferable given today's older first-birth ages (p18). I therefore center July-specific deviation near no additional effect, with a wide range for timing shifts and reporting noise.
assumptions.applies_when: July 2026 conceptions (roughly October 2025) faced similar Hinoeuma avoidance behavior to the January-May 2026 birth cohort.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp July-specific drop in pregnancy notifications or local July 2026 birth counts, or a renewed strong Hinoeuma avoidance signal beyond the survey evidence.

methods.rationale: Applies the observed January 2026 +0.5% yoy change (p16) to July 2025 total births. The role uses a change rate, not a level, and code converts the percent to a fraction. Failure mode: January's Hinoeuma timing and reporting conditions may not represent July; this ignores the May and trailing-12-month weakness.

methods.label: m5

p46.role: July 2025 total live births, all persons including foreign nationals

p54.role: Cumulative Jan-May 2026 total live births, all persons including foreign nationals, preliminary MHLW

p55.role: Cumulative Jan-May 2025 total live births, all persons including foreign nationals, preliminary MHLW

a1.role: July-specific additional change factor relative to the Jan-May 2026 trend, accounting for Hinoeuma/timing uncertainty

methods.rationale: Scales July 2025 total births by the Jan-May cumulative yoy trend and then applies a July-specific Hinoeuma/timing factor near 1. The survey evidence and muted Jan-May 2026 trend justify centering a1 near no additional effect while keeping a wide range. Shares p46, p54 and p55 with m2; a1 is the main judgment input.

methods.label: m6

p46.role: July 2025 total live births, all persons including foreign nationals

p56.role: Trailing 12-month total live births June 2025-May 2026, all persons including foreign nationals, preliminary MHLW

p57.role: Trailing 12-month total live births June 2024-May 2025, all persons including foreign nationals, preliminary MHLW

methods.rationale: Adjusts July 2025 total births by the trailing 12-month growth rate (p56/p57), a smoother recent trend signal than a single month. Failure mode: the trailing period ends in May 2026 and does not include July 2026, so any July-specific Hinoeuma or reporting effect is missed.

kept.rationale: The Jan-May 2026 cumulative all-person series is already +0.4% yoy (p54/p55), so any Hinoeuma effect in early 2026 births is muted. final.text:
The best estimate for live births occurring in Japan in July 2026, all persons including foreign nationals, as first reported in MHLW preliminary monthly vital statistics, is 62,449 birth (80% model-based interval 44,579 to 87,483 birth). This combines 6 methods at roughly equal weights, anchored on the observed July 2025 total of 62,521 births and adjusted by recent trends: the Jan-May 2026 cumulative of 282,222 births versus 280,979 births, May 2026 of 59,663 births versus 60,718 births, the January 2026 yoy change of 0.5%, and trailing-[n]-month totals 707,052 births and 709,893 births. The July 2025 anchor and these comparisons are observed; the July-specific Hinoeuma/timing factor 0.995 (range 0.8848 to 1.106) is an assumption. The interval reflects input uncertainty only, not demonstrated accuracy. The main risk is that July-specific Hinoeuma or reporting-timing effects differ from the early-2026 pattern. Better evidence would be a July-specific Hinoeuma survey or preliminary July reporting completeness data.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 July 2026 Hinoeuma/timing deviation factor relative to Jan-May 2026 trend: 0.995 fraction, range 0.8848 to 1.106 (range widened by code); used by m5. Overturned by: Evidence of a sharp July-specific drop in pregnancy notifications or local July 2026 birth counts, or a renewed strong Hinoeuma avoidance signal beyond the survey evidence.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
